title: Incidence and Outcomes of Human Adenovirus Infection and Disease in a Multicenter Cohort of Pediatric Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients.

analysis.scope_and_question: Human adenovirus (HAdV) among pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (allo-HCT) recipients can result in asymptomatic infection with risk for disease progression.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: There are limited data defining HAdV infection, disease, and case-fatality rates in a HAdV polymerase chain reaction (PCR) surveillance testing era. The current study aimed to define these outcomes using a priori definitions applied by a central review committee. Pediatric allo-HCT recipients were followed up for 180 days after HCT at 10 pediatric institutions. Blood and stool specimens were collected 0-7 days prior to allo-HCT for serum HAdV immunoglobulin G and stool HAdV PCR testing. Clinical data, including HAdV PCR testing results, informed central review committee-designated outcomes of HAdV infection, including DNAemia, disease, and deaths (case-fatality rate).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The HAdV infection and DNAemia incidence among surveilled patients was 27.1% and 16.0%, respectively. The incidence of proven or probable HAdV disease was 10.9% for the cohort and 12.6% for those under surveillance. The attributable case-fatality rate for those with proven or probable disease was 13.5%. HAdV infection and disease are common among pediatric allo-HCT recipients. HAdV disease is associated with a substantial HAdV-attributable mortality rate.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The HAdV infection incidence was highest (13 of 25 [52.0%]) in patients with pre-HCT HAdV immunoglobulin G and stool PCR positivity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Clinical trials assessing novel HAdV in pediatric allo-HCT recipients are needed.

analysis.summary_en: This review article examines the incidence and outcomes of human adenovirus (HAdV) infection and disease in pediatric allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (allo-HCT) recipients. The study highlights that HAdV infection and disease are common in this population, with a notable case-fatality rate for those with proven or probable disease. The research utilized a centralized review committee to define outcomes based on PCR testing and serology results, identifying high-risk patients through pretransplant testing. The findings underscore the need for clinical trials to develop novel interventions targeting HAdV in pediatric allo-HCT recipients.

title: A Virucidal And Endosomal Trapping Peptide Against Human Adenoviruses In Respiratory Organoids And Hamsters.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human adenoviruses (HAdVs) are common respiratory pathogens that cause severe, life-threatening infections in immunocompromised individuals and children. Despite their medical importance, no clinically approved antiviral drugs exist.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the antiviral activity of 4H30, a 4-branched human defensin peptide, against multiple HAdV subtypes in A549 and Calu-3 cells, as well as in human respiratory organoids and an immunosuppressed hamster model.
analysis.methods: Mechanistic studies demonstrated that 4H30 exhibited a unique dual mechanism of action: direct virucidal activity through capsid disruption and endosomal trapping by impairing protein VI-mediated membrane penetration.
analysis.main_results: Here, we showed that 4H30 exhibited broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple HAdV subtypes in A549 and Calu-3 cells with negligible cytotoxicity and a high barrier to viral resistance in A549 cells. Notably, 4H30 remained effective against HAdV-3 in human respiratory organoids and against HAdV-2 and HAdV-5 in an immunosuppressed hamster model, significantly reducing viral replication and disease-associated pathology.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings demonstrate that 4H30 can inhibit multiple HAdVs through a novel mechanism, offering a new therapeutic avenue against HAdV infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings offer a new therapeutic avenue against HAdV infections, particularly in immunocompromised individuals and children who are at higher risk of severe disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides strong evidence for the antiviral activity of 4H30 against multiple HAdV subtypes, but the evidence is limited to in vitro and animal models, which may not fully reflect human disease dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antiviral potential of 4H30, a human defensin peptide, against human adenoviruses (HAdVs). HAdVs are significant respiratory pathogens that cause severe infections in immunocompromised individuals and children, yet no approved antiviral drugs exist. The research demonstrates that 4H30 has broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple HAdV subtypes in cell lines and human respiratory organoids, as well as in an immunosuppressed hamster model, with negligible cytotoxicity. Mechanistic studies reveal that 4H30 acts through a dual mechanism: direct virucidal activity by disrupting the viral capsid and endosomal trapping by impairing protein VI-mediated membrane penetration. These findings suggest a novel therapeutic approach for HAdV infections. However, the study is limited to in vitro and animal models, which may not fully capture human disease complexity. The evidence is strong for the antiviral activity of 4H30 but requires further validation in clinical settings.

title: Efficacy of alcohol-based hand rubs against human adenovirus on contaminated hands.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Viruses significantly contribute to outbreaks in healthcare facilities, primarily through direct or indirect hand contact. Consequently, hand disinfection using hygienic hand rubs is a pivotal measure for preventing nosocomial virus infections in medical environments.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the in vivo efficacy of various ethanol formulations and two commercially available alcohol mixtures against human adenovirus type 5 (AdV-5) using a cross-over study design based on EN 17430.
analysis.methods: The study utilized a cross-over design based on EN 17430 to evaluate the in vivo efficacy of pure ethanol formulations in concentrations from 60% to 97% and two alcohol mixtures (M1: 45% ethanol and 18% 1-propanol; M2: 45% 2-propanol and 30% 1-propanol) on the hands of 5 or 20 volunteers.
analysis.main_results: With the different ethanol formulations increasing reduction factors with higher alcohol concentrations were detected. Of the two alcohol-containing mixtures, only M1 demonstrated efficacy based on the requirements of EN 17430, the second formulation M2, however, narrowly failed effectiveness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Results from suspension tests with AdV-5 were not directly transferable to those obtained with the alcohol formulations tested under practical conditions as per EN 17430.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against the direct transferability of results from suspension tests to practical conditions, emphasizing the need for in vivo evaluation of hand rubs for preventing AdV-5 infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations include the small sample size and the use of a cross-over design, which may introduce bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the efficacy of various ethanol formulations and alcohol mixtures against human adenovirus type 5 (AdV-5) using a cross-over design. Results showed that only one mixture met the EN 17430 requirements, highlighting the need for in vivo evaluation over suspension tests.

title: A Confirmatory, Dual Center Nonhuman Primate Study on the Efficacy of Novel Oropharyngeal Spray Immunization With an Adenoviral Vector Vaccine Against RSV-Important Lessons Learned.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background In a randomized, blinded, dual center study across two European primate research facilities, we evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime-oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: Methods Rhesus macaques received an RSV fusion protein (F) DNA vaccine via electroporation, followed by two mucosal administrations of a recombinant adenovirus vector encoding the same antigen. Mock-vaccinated animals and a comparator group mimicking natural immunity induced by primary RSV infection were included as controls.
analysis.methods: Systemic and mucosal immune responses were monitored longitudinally.
analysis.main_results: Results We detected robust cellular and humoral immune responses, but with some variability between the two centers. Nevertheless, RSV-vaccinated animals demonstrated markedly reduced viral replication in the upper and lower respiratory tract after RSV challenge infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Conclusion Our results support the potential of mucosal adenoviral boosting following DNA priming to induce protective immunity against RSV, while highlighting challenges associated with multi-center preclinical vaccine studies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Our findings suggest that mucosal adenoviral boosting could be a viable strategy for RSV vaccine development, with implications for improving immunization protocols and addressing challenges in multi-center trials.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Unexpected RSV-specific immunity in the control group at one single study site prevented confirmation of the predefined primary endpoint.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of a DNA prime-oropharyngeal adenoviral boost vaccination strategy against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in a dual-center, randomized, blinded trial involving rhesus macaques. The DNA vaccine was administered via electroporation, followed by mucosal adenoviral boosters encoding the RSV fusion protein (F). Control groups included mock-vaccinated animals and those mimicking natural immunity from primary RSV infection. The study observed robust immune responses but noted variability between centers. RSV-vaccinated animals showed reduced viral replication in the respiratory tract after challenge. However, unexpected immunity in the control group at one site hindered confirmation of the primary endpoint. The results suggest that mucosal adenoviral boosting may be effective for RSV vaccine development, but multi-center trials face challenges. These findings have implications for improving vaccine strategies and addressing limitations in preclinical research.

title: The evolving landscape of hybrid viral vector architectures: a persisting niche

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the challenges and constraints in the evolution of hybrid viral vector systems, particularly in relation to biological and technological barriers that hinder their development and application. The background highlights the need to overcome limitations of individual viral platforms, such as restricted payload capacity and limited control over genomic persistence.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review examining the architectural principles of hybrid vector design, focusing on the evolution of these systems as a logical extension of viral engineering strategies rather than a response to non-viral platforms. It analyzes various structural configurations and their associated trade-offs.
analysis.methods: The review outlines the integration of functional modules from diverse viral and non-viral systems to expand therapeutic potential. It also discusses the biological and technological trade-offs of increased structural complexity, including manufacturing constraints, immunogenicity, and regulatory challenges.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights key structural configurations such as adenoviral, lentiviral, herpes simplex virus (HSV) amplicon, baculoviral, and bacteriophage-derived chimeras, as well as their integration with transposon systems. It also identifies potential limiting factors such as reduced efficiency, incompatibility between packaging and replication mechanisms, and immunological burden.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that hybrid vector systems represent a modular and evolving design paradigm that complements advances in monoplatform vectors. They note that while these systems offer potential, their clinical translation has been limited due to the challenges associated with their complexity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the ongoing development of hybrid vector systems as a valuable approach for addressing complex therapeutic challenges, such as those requiring expanded capacity, multifunctionality, or combinatorial control of gene delivery outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges limitations such as reduced efficiency with increasing complexity, incompatibility between viral platforms, and immunological constraints. The evidence is based on a review of existing literature and is considered to have moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the challenges and constraints in the evolution of hybrid viral vector systems, emphasizing biological and technological barriers that hinder their development. It highlights the modular design of these vectors and their potential to expand therapeutic applications. The study notes that while hybrid systems offer advantages, their clinical translation has been limited due to complexity-related issues. The findings suggest that hybrid vectors remain a valuable approach for addressing complex gene delivery needs, despite the difficulties in achieving linear performance improvements. The review also identifies key structural configurations and trade-offs, such as manufacturing constraints and immunogenicity, which affect their practical application. The evidence is based on a comprehensive analysis of existing literature and is considered to have moderate confidence due to the limitations in the integration of heterologous modules and the challenges in achieving coordinated expression.

title: Rare Adenoviral Vectored Vaccines for Emerging Influenza Threats

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate recombinant adenovirus serotypes 4, 28, and 48 expressing a centralized H5 influenza hemagglutinin consensus antigen as next-generation vectors for broad, single-dose protection against diverse H5 influenza clades. This addresses the limitations of current vaccine platforms, such as waning immunity and restricted antigenic breadth.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved mice receiving a single intramuscular or intranasal vaccination with recombinant adenoviruses expressing a centralized H5 influenza hemagglutinin consensus antigen, followed by challenge with diverse, lethal H5N1 viruses two weeks later.
analysis.methods: The H5 centralized consensus vaccine was designed using human sequences from the 2003–2006 bird flu outbreak and cloned into four low-prevalence recombinant adenoviruses. Immune correlates, survival, and protection from challenge-associated weight loss were assessed.
analysis.main_results: Vaccinated mice were largely protected from lethal challenge against strains spanning twenty years of influenza evolution. Both vaccination routes conferred complete protection against antigenically related strains and strong protection against more divergent clade 2.3.4.4b strains. Protection occurred before neutralizing antibodies could be detected, although strong H5 antibody responses were induced by all vaccines.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Adenovirus vectors expressing a centralized H5 consensus hemagglutinin elicit rapid, broad protection against diverse H5 influenza viruses following a single intramuscular or intranasal immunization. These results support the continued development of low-seroprevalence adenoviral vectors as a next-generation influenza vaccine platform for rapidly emerging influenza viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform the development of rapid, broad-spectrum influenza vaccines that could be deployed to protect against emerging influenza strains, potentially reducing the impact of future pandemics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the use of a single animal model and the lack of human data. The evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of human trials and the need for further validation in clinical settings.

analysis.summary_en: The study evaluated recombinant adenovirus vectors expressing a centralized H5 influenza hemagglutinin consensus antigen for broad protection against diverse H5 influenza strains in mice. Vaccinated mice were largely protected from lethal challenge, supporting the development of these vectors as a next-generation influenza vaccine platform.

title: Adenovirus early proteins E1A and E3-19K reveal separable regulatory states of the ER stress sensor IRE1a.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to elucidate the mechanisms by which human adenovirus preferentially activates the IRE1a-XBP1 pathway during infection, addressing a knowledge gap in understanding the selective activation of this pathway by viral proteins.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved molecular and cellular analyses of human adenovirus early proteins E1A and E3-19K, focusing on their interactions with the ER stress sensor IRE1a and its role in viral infection.
analysis.methods: The researchers used biochemical and molecular techniques to detect and characterize the interactions between E1A, E3-19K, and IRE1a, including the formation of complexes and their effects on BiP dissociation and XBP1 splicing.
analysis.main_results: Both E1A and E3-19K were detected in IRE1a-containing complexes, demonstrating a stepwise regulation of IRE1a by these viral proteins during infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal that human adenovirus employs distinct early proteins to regulate IRE1a in separate steps, showing that canonical IRE1a activation hallmarks can be mechanistically separated during viral infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the molecular mechanisms of human adenovirus-induced ER stress responses, which could inform future studies on viral pathogenesis and the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and molecular analyses, and the evidence is based on biochemical interactions, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how human adenovirus selectively activates the IRE1a-XBP1 pathway through its early proteins E1A and E3-19K. The research demonstrates that these proteins dissociate BiP from IRE1a in distinct steps, leading to separate signaling outcomes. The findings highlight the mechanistic separation of IRE1a activation during viral infection, offering new insights into adenovirus pathogenesis. While the study provides valuable molecular data, its reliance on in vitro methods limits the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength, as it is based on biochemical interactions rather than comprehensive in vivo observations.

title: A neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting species B adenoviruses largely mimics the DSG2 receptor engagement mechanism

analysis.research_question_and_background: Species B human adenoviruses, including HAdV7, HAdV3, and the re-emerging HAdV55, cause severe respiratory disease and engage desmoglein-2 (DSG2) through their fiber knob.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we report the identification and structural characterization of two monoclonal antibodies, 5C5 and 6G7, raised against the HAdV7 fiber knob.
analysis.methods: Both antibodies neutralize HAdV7 and display cross-reactivity toward other B-HAdVs, with nanomolar affinities.
analysis.main_results: Notably, 5C5 recognizes HAdV3 despite limited sequence conservation and exhibits greater neutralization potency than 6G7.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Cryo-electron microscopy structures at 1.8 Å and 2.0 Å resolution for 6G7 and 5C5 respectively, reveal distinct binding modes: 6G7 engages the trimeric fiber knob at a 3:3 antibody: knob ratio, whereas 5C5 binds the apex at a 1:3 ratio.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The 5C5 epitope overlaps with key DSG2-interacting residues, including a conserved pocket among B-HAdVs, providing a structural basis for its enhanced neutralization through receptor-binding blockade.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings establish the fiber knob apex as a vulnerable site for antibody-mediated neutralization and identify 5C5 as a candidate targeting pathogenic species B adenoviruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the neutralizing mechanisms of two monoclonal antibodies, 5C5 and 6G7, against species B human adenoviruses (B-HAdVs), including HAdV7, HAdV3, and HAdV55. The research focuses on understanding how these antibodies interact with the fiber knob of B-HAdVs, particularly the DSG2 receptor. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals distinct binding modes, with 5C5 showing greater neutralization potency and targeting a conserved receptor-binding site. These findings highlight the fiber knob apex as a potential target for antibody-based therapies against pathogenic B-HAdVs. The study contributes to the development of broad-spectrum neutralizing agents and provides structural insights into receptor engagement mechanisms. However, the results are limited to the specific antibodies and B-HAdVs studied, and further research is needed to validate their efficacy against other strains.
